title: Microsoft Teams: Intelligent call delegation answers and screens incoming calls
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, licensing, billing prerequisites and documented controls are supported. One minor correction remains: the checklist asks administrators to configure Auto-apply new services, but that control is not represented in the controls table.

claims.claim: Intelligent call delegation is an AI-powered voice agent for incoming Microsoft Teams calls.
claims.quote: Intelligent call delegation in Microsoft Teams is an AI-powered voice agent that helps users manage incoming calls.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The voice agent answers calls on the user's behalf when turned on.
claims.quote: When users turn on Intelligent call delegation, the voice agent answers calls on their behalf.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The agent collects the caller's reason for calling.
claims.quote: Screen incoming calls and collect the caller's reason for calling.

claims.claim: The agent takes action based on the user's availability and settings.
claims.quote: It answers calls on users' behalf, gathers context about the caller's intent, and takes action based on users' availability and settings.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The agent can screen incoming calls before connecting them.
claims.quote: Screen calls before connecting | Controls whether Intelligent call delegation screens calls and provides context before connecting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The agent can route urgent calls to the user.
claims.quote: Route urgent calls to the user and provide context about the call.

claims.claim: The agent can schedule follow-up appointments through Microsoft Bookings.
claims.quote: It can screen calls, route urgent calls to users, and schedule follow-up appointments through Microsoft Bookings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Callers are told they are speaking with an attendant rather than a person.
claims.quote: Callers are informed that they're speaking with an attendant rather than a person.

claims.quote: Public preview uses usage-based billing (UBB) with Copilot Credits.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Frontier preview tenants lose incoming call screening if spending is not configured.
claims.quote: If spending is not configured, tenants coming from Frontier preview will no longer have incoming calls screened by this feature.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not separately stated arrival behavior for non-Frontier tenants without a spending policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" "spending policy" "Frontier"; "Intelligent call delegation" "no spending policy". Read feature prerequisites, billing overview and both supplied notices; explicit loss-of-screening wording covers Frontier tenants only.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators must set up usage-based billing and create a spending policy for this feature in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins must set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and create a spending policy for Intelligent call delegation in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; controls[4].note
claims.claim: The feature's spending policy should select only Intelligent call delegation under Agents and services and clear other selections.
claims.quote: When you create the spending policy, under Agents and services, ensure that only Intelligent call delegation is selected. Clear the checkboxes for all other services.

claims.claim: Administrators should choose the intended user and group scope before assigning the spending policy.
claims.quote: When you select users and groups, choose the appropriate scope before assigning the policy.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects metered Copilot Credit consumption.
claims.quote: Intelligent call delegation uses usage-based billing with Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: A limited monthly budget limits the credits a spending policy can spend each month.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: Users hitting the limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Credits reset on the first of the month under the spending-policy limits guidance.
claims.quote: until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: The spending-policy page's general per-user monthly limit guidance is at least 2,000 credits.
claims.quote: Monthly budget limit for users: Set at least 2,000 credits per user per month

claims.claim: A spending policy uses prepaid credits before pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: The policy always uses prepaid credits first, whether through capacity packs or through pre-purchase plans, before moving to pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: Feature-specific billing arrangements for General Availability are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" "General Availability" billing; "Intelligent call delegation" billing general availability January 2027 pricing. Read feature page, billing overview and supplied notices; published feature billing describes the public preview.

claims.claim: The feature page does not further define which licences count beyond its Microsoft Copilot licence prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" "Which licenses". Read the complete Manage Intelligent call delegation feature page, particularly Prerequisites; it requires a Microsoft Copilot license without defining qualifying SKUs.

claims.where: Open questions: saved recordings and transcripts
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page names recording and transcription settings but not storage location or access permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" recordings transcripts stored access. Read complete feature page and search excerpts; its Policy settings table describes saving recordings/transcripts, not storage location or access permissions.

claims.claim: The availability switch is at Teams admin center > Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies > policy > General > Enable Intelligent call delegation.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Under General, turn Enable Intelligent call delegation on or off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity <policy name> -PersonalAttendant Disabled disables personal attendant for users with that policy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy
    [-Identity <string>]
    [-PersonalAttendant <string>]
-PersonalAttendant
Enables the user to use the personal attendant
Disabled: The user is not enabled to use this functionality.

claims.claim: The PSTN caller control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies > policy > Choose which calls Intelligent call delegation answers > External PSTN calls.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Choose which calls Intelligent call delegation answers; External PSTN calls

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity <policy name> -InboundPSTNCalls Disabled disables personal attendant for incoming PSTN calls.
claims.quote:
[-Identity <string>]
[-InboundPSTNCalls <string>]
-InboundPSTNCalls
Enables the user to use the personal attendant for incoming PSTN calls
Disabled: The user is not enabled to use this functionality.

claims.claim: Calendar access is at Teams admin center > Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies > policy > Choose what Intelligent call delegation can do > Calendar integration.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Choose what Intelligent call delegation can do; Calendar integration

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity <policy name> -CalendarBookings Disabled disables the personal attendant calendar functionality.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity SalesPersonalAttendantPolicy -CalendarBookings Disabled
Sets the value of the parameter CalendarBookings to Disabled in the Teams Personal Attendant Policy instance called SalesPersonalAttendantPolicy.

claims.claim: Automatic recording is at Teams admin center > Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies > policy > Manage recording and transcription > Automatically save recording.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Intelligent call delegation policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Manage recording and transcription; Automatically save recording

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AutomaticRecording Disabled disables automatic saving of personal attendant call recordings.
claims.quote:
[-Identity <string>]
[-AutomaticRecording <string>]
-AutomaticRecording
Enables the user to use the automatic storing of personal attendant call recordings
Disabled: The user is not enabled to use this functionality.

claims.claim: Spending limits are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Spending limits.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab. Select the spending policy you want to edit. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: Scope; Agents and services; Billing method; Spending limits

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} can update spending limits through periodLimit or perUserLimit.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b
The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy assigns a policy to users or groups.
claims.quote: Assigns a specific Teams Personal Attendant Policy to a user, a group of users, or sets the Global policy instance.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams Set cmdlet exposes InboundFederatedCalls and InboundInternalCalls for the other caller types, with EnabledUserOverride, Enabled and Disabled values.
claims.quote: -InboundFederatedCalls: Enables the user to use the personal attendant for incoming calls from other domains. -InboundInternalCalls: Enables the user to use the personal attendant for incoming domain calls. Possible values: EnabledUserOverride; Enabled; Disabled.

claims.claim: The feature page's New-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy example uses CalendarBookings Disabled to disable calendar integration.
claims.quote:
The following command creates a new policy named SalesPersonalAttendantPolicy with calendar integration for scheduling follow-ups disabled.
New-CsTeamsPersonalAttendantPolicy -Identity SalesPersonalAttendantPolicy -CalendarBookings Disabled

claims.claim: AutomaticTranscription is the Set cmdlet parameter for automatic transcript saving.
claims.quote:
-AutomaticTranscription
Enables the user to use the automatic storing of personal attendant call transcriptions

claims.claim: The spending-policy update API is beta and lists displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods as updatable properties.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported. The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The spending-policy creation entry point is + Add spending policy under Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: Turning off Auto-apply new services prevents future supported services and agents from automatically joining the spending policy.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included. Administrators must review and add the new services and agents to the policy.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management provides credit-consumption review against spending limits and alert thresholds.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells readers to configure appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Switch off Auto-apply new services on the spending policy". The spending-policy table row governs "Spending limits" and contains no Auto-apply new services setting.
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout checklist bullet beginning "Switch off Auto-apply new services"; that setting has no corresponding control row.
